items.headline: Ministers Shanmugam and Tan See Leng each awarded S$145,000 in legal costs from Bloomberg
items.summary: A Singapore court awarded Senior Minister K. Shanmugam and Manpower Minister Tan See Leng about S$145,000 each in legal costs after winning their defamation suit over a Bloomberg article, on top of S$230,000 each in damages.

items.headline: Police and IMDA investigate Massive Attack after 'Free Palestine' chant at Singapore concert
items.summary: Singapore police and the IMDA opened investigations after Massive Attack chanted 'Free Palestine' and held a Palestinian flag at The Star Performing Arts Centre.

items.headline: Singapore scraps the 15-month wait-out barring private owners from buying resale HDB flats
items.summary: Chee Hong Tat said private property owners buying a non-subsidised resale HDB flat without an HDB loan will no longer face the 15-month wait-out imposed in 2022.

items.headline: Every Singapore household to get an extra S$300 in CDC vouchers in January 2027
items.summary: Second Minister for Finance Jeffrey Siow announced a roughly S$900 million cost-of-living package giving every household an extra S$300 in CDC vouchers in January 2027.

items.headline: MAS tightens policy for a second straight quarter, sees inflation elevated into 2027
items.summary: The Monetary Authority of Singapore again allowed a stronger Singapore dollar in July, holding 2026 inflation forecasts at 1.5-2.5% and warning inflation eases only in H2 2027.

items.headline: India doubles prison terms for exam-paper leaks after 'Cockroach party' protests
items.summary: India's parliament passed a law doubling the maximum prison term for exam-paper leaks to 10 years and raising fines above 10 million rupees, a concession to the Cockroach Janta Party movement.

items.headline: India's Supreme Court orders the release of minors detained in the Cockroach protests
items.summary: The Supreme Court ordered states to free under-18s arrested in the Cockroach Janta Party protests without prior records, and to preserve drone, body-camera and CCTV footage of the crackdown.

items.headline: Rising US Treasury yields complicate the RBI's defence of a near-record-low rupee
items.summary: Bloomberg reported that a climb in US Treasury yields is complicating the RBI's strategy on rates and the rupee, which is recovering from a record low amid US-Iran tensions and pricey oil.

items.headline: India's Nifty 50 heads for a monthly gain as trade deals offset monsoon worries
items.summary: The Nifty 50 looked set to close July higher in muted trade as investors weighed India-US and India-EU trade deals against a delayed monsoon and results from Sun Pharma, Maruti and ITC.

items.headline: Chancellor John Healey to deliver his first Budget on October 28
items.summary: Chancellor John Healey confirmed he will present his first Autumn Budget on Oct 28, a test for PM Andy Burnham amid a reported GBP4.7bn defence-funding gap and costly pledges.

items.headline: Burnham to hand English metro mayors a share of income tax and business rates
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham said metro mayors will keep a share of locally generated income tax and business rates in a devolution push, with details in a roadmap alongside the autumn Budget.

items.headline: UK house prices edge up 0.1% in July, the first gain in three months
items.summary: Nationwide said UK house prices rose 0.1% in July to an average GBP277,542, the first monthly gain in three months and in line with forecasts.

items.headline: Burnham presses for welfare cuts as Labour MPs warn against 'punitive' reform
items.summary: PM Andy Burnham said Britain must get 'really serious' about cutting a soaring welfare bill by making some support conditional on training and work, drawing Labour MP warnings.

items.headline: US strikes Iran as Tehran retaliates against Kuwait and Jordan
items.summary: US forces hit dozens of IRGC targets across Iran; Iran retaliated with a drone strike on Kuwait's Ahmad al-Jaber airbase area that killed one worker, while Jordan intercepted five missiles.

items.headline: Egypt is drawn into the Iran war as a drone hits a US-owned LNG tanker at Damietta
items.summary: A drone struck the US-owned LNG facility Energos Winter at Egypt's Damietta port, igniting a fire that spread to a second ship; Iran distanced itself, calling Egypt 'an important friend'.

items.headline: Update: Saudi Arabia forms a 14-nation Maritime Defence Alliance to guard shipping lanes
items.summary: Saudi Arabia announced a Multinational Maritime Defense Alliance with 13 other states, including Turkey, Egypt, Pakistan and Qatar, to protect the Red Sea, Bab al-Mandeb and Strait of Hormuz.

items.headline: Trump announces a phased Hamas disarmament deal, with Israeli withdrawal to follow
items.summary: Trump said his Board of Peace reached a deal for Hamas and other factions to disarm in phases for a staged Israeli withdrawal, with a roadmap due in 14 days; Hamas set conditions and no final deal is confirmed.

items.headline: At least 57 die as tens of thousands breach the Morocco-Ceuta border into Spain
items.summary: At least 57 migrants died, many drowning or crushed near Tarajal beach, as roughly 50,000 surged toward Spain's enclave of Ceuta; Sanchez visited, the military deployed, and most were sent back.

items.headline: Samsung and SK Hynix post record quarterly profits on AI memory demand
items.summary: Samsung and SK Hynix, about 80% of the memory market, booked roughly 150 trillion won (about US$104 billion) in combined operating profit in Q2, with SK Hynix's operating profit up nearly 557% year on year.

items.headline: Microsoft jumps about 15% as Azure cloud growth beats estimates
items.summary: Microsoft shares rose roughly 15% after fiscal Q4 results showed faster-than-expected Azure cloud growth, reinforcing confidence in AI-infrastructure spending.

items.headline: Meta's free cash flow collapses to $784 million as AI capex surges
items.summary: Meta's quarterly free cash flow fell to $784 million, its lowest in nearly four years, as capex soared; it lifted 2026 capex guidance's low end to $130-145 billion and the stock fell about 8%.

items.headline: Bloomberg: China's Moonshot runs its Kimi model on a 20,000-chip Nvidia cluster via Alibaba
items.summary: Bloomberg reported Moonshot built its Kimi model on a roughly 20,000-chip Nvidia cluster obtained through investor Alibaba, testing US export controls; Alibaba denied supplying the chips.

items.headline: Wall Street closes July higher as the Dow logs a fourth straight winning month
items.summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.7% to 7,489.72, the Nasdaq gained 1% to 25,373.85 and the Dow added 276.97 points to 52,485.03 on Friday, the Dow's fourth straight monthly gain despite a roughly 7% July drop in the Nasdaq-100.

items.headline: Chevron beats on a war-driven oil rally while Exxon misses on refining
items.summary: Chevron posted adjusted EPS of $6.06 (vs $5.56 expected) and about $70 billion revenue, its biggest net income since 2022, while Exxon's $3.52 adjusted EPS slightly missed on refining troubles.

items.headline: Gold climbs toward $4,100 an ounce, set for its first monthly gain since February
items.summary: Gold rose toward $4,100 an ounce on Friday, with spot bullion around $4,040, on track for its first monthly advance since February on geopolitical risk and inflation hedging.

items.headline: NYSE parent ICE agrees to buy MarketAxess for about $6 billion
items.summary: Intercontinental Exchange agreed to buy fixed-income trading platform MarketAxess for roughly $6 billion at $167 a share, a premium of about a third, expanding its bond-trading business.

items.headline: Blackstone to buy a $25 billion HSBC Australia loan portfolio
items.summary: Blackstone agreed to acquire an A$36 billion (about US$25 billion) Australian home and personal loan book from HSBC, one of the largest such transactions on record.

items.headline: Nakashima upsets defending champion de Minaur to reach the Washington semifinals
items.summary: Brandon Nakashima beat top seed and defending champion Alex de Minaur 7-6(5), 3-6, 6-4 in the DC Open quarterfinals to reach the semifinals.

items.headline: Pegula beats Kalinskaya again to return to the Washington semifinals
items.summary: Jessica Pegula beat Anna Kalinskaya, for the sixth time in seven meetings, in the DC Open quarterfinals to reach the Washington semifinals for the first time since 2023.

items.headline: Trent Rockets beat Manchester Super Giants by six wickets as Finn Allen hits 72*
items.summary: In The Hundred men's competition at Manchester, Trent Rockets chased 138 with 13 balls to spare to win by six wickets, Finn Allen the player of the match on 72 not out off 35 balls.

items.headline: Trent Rockets women win by 31 runs as Sophia Dunkley makes 57
items.summary: In The Hundred women's competition at Manchester, Trent Rockets made 153 for 8 and bowled out Manchester Super Giants for 122 to win by 31 runs, Sophia Dunkley player of the match on 57.

items.headline: Verstappen's Red Bull exit clause is in play as he sits seventh at the summer break
items.summary: With F1 on its summer break after Hungary, Max Verstappen, seventh and outside the top two, can trigger a clause allowing a 2027 move; boss Laurent Mekies said the team must prove he should stay.

items.headline: Chilean mummies yield the oldest smallpox genomes ever found in the Americas
items.summary: DNA from two mummified people at Camarones 9 in northern Chile, who died between 1492 and 1631, gave the first ancient smallpox genomes from the Americas; published in Science, they confirm a European colonial origin.

items.headline: NASA opens a new Flight Dynamics Research Facility wind tunnel at Langley
items.summary: NASA opened its Flight Dynamics Research Facility in Hampton, Virginia, a 25,000-square-foot vertical wind tunnel with a 20-foot test chamber that replaces two historic Langley tunnels.

items.headline: Nature examines the faint 'biophoton' glow that all living things emit
items.summary: A Nature feature reviews evidence that living cells emit an ultra-weak glow of photons that tracks their health, raising the prospect of non-invasive disease diagnostics.

items.headline: Astronomers capture the best image yet of Betelgeuse's hidden companion star
items.summary: Using the VLT's SPHERE instrument, astronomers imaged Betelgeuse's faint companion, nicknamed Siwarha, at 6.1-sigma confidence, helping explain the star's roughly six-year brightness cycle.

fun_fact.headline: The fax machine was invented before the telephone
fun_fact.body: The fax machine is older than the telephone. Alexander Bain patented a facsimile device in 1843, about 33 years before Bell patented the telephone in 1876.

puzzle.title: The Vowel Rule
puzzle.body: Four cards show A, K, 2, 7 (letter on one side, number on the other). Claim: if a card has a vowel on one side, it has an even number on the other. Which cards must you turn over?
puzzle.approach: Test only what could break the rule.
puzzle.answer: A and 7 only. A must have an even number behind it; 7 must not have a vowel behind it. K and 2 cannot disprove the rule. (Wason selection task.)

word_puzzle.title: Building Blocks
word_puzzle.body: Sort 16 words into 4 groups of 4 by the hidden word each can precede (STONE / LIGHT / FLOWER / HOUSE).
word_puzzle.approach: Ask what single word could follow each entry.
word_puzzle.answer: STONE: LIME, MILE, BRIM, GEM | LIGHT: MOON, SPOT, SUN, DAY | FLOWER: CORN, MAY, WILD, WALL | HOUSE: GREEN, WARE, FARM, PENT.
